title: Janapada of Cedī
capsule: Cedī (also Chedi or Cheti) was an ancient Indian janapada listed in the Anguttara Nikāya among the sixteen great states, occupying the Yamuna-Vindhya zone of central India corresponding roughly to modern Bundelkhand in Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh, with its capital Śuktimātī on the Śukti river. It figures prominently in the Mahābhārata as the kingdom of King Śiśupāla, a cousin and rival of Krishna slain at the Rājasūya sacrifice of Yudhiṣṭhira, and appears in Buddhist texts as a territory visited by the Buddha. The state faded from major political significance by the mid-first millennium BCE and was eventually absorbed within the Maurya imperial system.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Cedī's location in the Bundelkhand region is broadly agreed in scholarship, but precise territorial limits are inferred entirely from Puranic and epic textual references with no contemporaneous archaeological demarcation.
